draft.title: Scientific names
card: Common names change from place to place. One animal can have several names, and one name can be used for different animals.
Each species has a scientific name made of two parts. The first part is its genus. The second part is its species.
The name is written in Latin form. The genus starts with a capital letter, the species starts with a small letter, and both are in italics, such as Homo sapiens.
Scientists everywhere use the same scientific name for a species. This stops confusion between languages and regions.
draft.remember: A scientific name has two parts, genus then species, and it is the same worldwide.

a.q: Why do scientists give each species a two-part scientific name?
opts: So every scientist names the species the same way
So the name can show the animal's size and colour
So each region can keep its own name for the species
So the species can be sorted into a kingdom by name
a.why: A scientific name is shared by scientists everywhere, so they all know which species is meant. Common names can differ between places, so they do not give this certainty.
a.clue: Think about what goes wrong when names change from place to place.

b.q: A student writes the name of the koala as Phascolarctos cinereus. Which part of this name is the genus?
opts: Neither part, as it is only a common name
b.why: The genus is always the first part of a scientific name, and it starts with a capital letter. The second part, cinereus, names the species within that genus. It is tempting to pick both parts, but the full name is the genus and species together.
b.clue: Look at which word has the capital letter.

a.best: So every scientist names the species the same way
